subject.title: v2026.6.8: plugin_state_entries SQLite database corruption — session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released

question: Should OpenClaw add availability-first malformed openclaw.sqlite quarantine/recovery now, first prove the takeover-to-corruption cause, or split recovery and session-lock prevention into separate canonical work?
rationale: The source boundary is clear, but the right behavior changes data-retention, startup availability, WAL/checkpoint, and session-lock policy for a shared persisted store used by multiple runtime surfaces.

options.title: Define shared-state recovery first
options.body: Choose quarantine/preserve/fresh-state semantics for malformed openclaw.sqlite, then implement recovery with plugin-state and task-state regression proof while preserving corrupted files for analysis.

options.title: Prove corruption cause first
options.body: Keep fail-closed shared-state behavior while maintainers collect preserved DB sidecars, integrity traces, and a live takeover-to-corruption reproduction.

options.title: Split the work
options.body: Track shared SQLite recovery in the existing malformed-state thread and keep this issue focused on the session-lock/WAL causality evidence for plugin_state_entries corruption.

recommendation.title: Define shared-state recovery first
recommendation.body: Choose quarantine/preserve/fresh-state semantics for malformed openclaw.sqlite, then implement recovery with plugin-state and task-state regression proof while preserving corrupted files for analysis.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest ownership signal is the database-first refactor and shared SQLite source-of-truth boundary introduced through PR 78595.
